recipes.name: Across the Border Tequila Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds medium shrimp - peeled and deveined

steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic; cook and stir, about 30 seconds. Add shrimp; cook and stir until pink, about 3 minutes. Add tequila and lime juice; season with salt and chili powder. Simmer until liquid has evaporated, about 3 minutes more.
Pour shrimp on a serving plate; garnish with cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

raw_recipe.headline: Across the Border Tequila Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: This across the border tequila shrimp recipe is quite easy — sauté shrimp and garlic in butter then simmer it with tequila, lime juice, and chili powder.

review.reviewBody: This Tequila Shrimp was very yummy!! I have been making it for about 6 months now and have made just a few changes. I melt the butter at the lowest heat setting then once melted I sift about 1/2tsp to 1tsp cornstarch to the butter and stir untill most of the cornstarch is blended with the butter (to make a rue). Another thing I have done is added 1/4 tsp Cheyenne pepper to the mixture along with the salt and chili pepper.those were the only changes I made to it and its GREAT!! My Hubby is a picky eater and he gave me the 2 thumbs up and even asks me to make it for dinner. I have also let my God son try it and he LOVES it and always asks for 2nd's (which is rare!!). I hope my comment helps anyone out there wanting to try it or who has already tried it but wanted to try something a little different.

Amazing!! Was way better than my expectation. I added ground cumin and doubled the tequila and lime juice. I also put in 2 tsp of cornstarch to thicken the sauce which I highly recommend. Served over Parmesan couscous and it was divine

this was so delicious.. i didn't follow the directions and used this more as a marinade/cooking liquid.. left out the butter.. put everything in a zip lock bag and marinated for about 30 min's.. used mahi mahi fillets, doubled the chili powder, and subbed bottled lemon juice for the lime.. poured everything into a pan and cooked until done.. used the leftover juice to pour over rice.. ty so much for the recipe

Hubby and I love this recipe. I make it with a lime jalapeno cilantro rice and fresh corn, cut from cob and sauteed in butter and sprinkled with chili powder.
If I have some crusty bread to serve with this, I make more of the sauce and don't let it completely cook down, so we can dip the bread. Sooo good!

This literally could not be easier or more delicious. I took a few cues from other reviewers and mixed a tablespoon of cornstarch in with the butter as I melted it at a low temperature and the sauce was a perfect consistency. I also served it over couscous (I had no rice) with sliced avocado. I'm not a big tequila drinker so I purchased a very small bottle of Patron Silver for $6.00 just to make this and it was well worth it. I also must admit I had a little shot as a was cooking, which should be mandatory, as it added to the whole experience. My husband and I were both in love with this shrimp and it will most certainly become part of my dinner repertoire.

Maybe I did something wrong but I didn't care for this recipe at all. I think 6 minutes total is too long to cook shrimp for, and I think 6 minutes isn't enough time to infuse the shrimp with any of the lime tequila flavor. Maybe if I marinated the shrimp beforehand in the tequila, lime, garlic and chili powder and then cooked it quickly in the butter it would work better. The way the recipe was written, I feel like while the aroma was amazing, the shrimp was overcooked and had no flavor.

Please, DON'T SIMMER UNTIL LIQUID EVAPORATES! With that much butter and almost half a cup of liquid from the tequila and lime juice, plus the shrimp's liquid, your medium shrimp will be very overcooked. Aside from cooking just until the shrimp were done, I followed this recipe almost exactly and we really enjoyed the dish. I did use chipotle powder instead of chili powder and added the chopped cilantro with the pepper to cook down a little. Thanks for sharing.

Found it a bit weak in flavour so added some dried red pepper chilies and then removed shrimp as soon as they were cooked and kept them warm while I reduced the liquid and used it over the top. Set shrimp on top of lime cilantro rice that had been put in a mold ring.

This is a great summer recipe- very light. I tossed cilantro in the sauce at the end ( I love cilantro! ) and let it blend in, and served it over rice. I also double the sauce to have lots for the rice to soak up.

Delicious! This has become a staple in my household. I serve it with rice, black beans, sauteed peppers and onion (fajita style) and a half an avocado per person. It's a simple meal to prepare and it's one of my boyfriend's favorite dishes. Thank you so much for sharing this one!

After I messed with this, it is definatly a 5. I made as listed, but the liquid wasnt evaporating and was very watery and didn't have much taste (I'm assuming the shrimp was really watery??) Anyway, I dumped out half of my liquid and then readded in the tequila and lime juice (1/2 recipe amounts) and dumped in more chile powder and garlic salt to taste. Taste was great, but still thought it was too thin, so I sprinkled some flour over the shrimp and stirred in. The shrimp and thickened sauce could go inside wraps.
I like to add corn starch & extra lime to my shrimp. Great recipe.
Delicious! I followed recipe as written. Perfect! I certainly will make it again. For company, it was that good and just for us, it was that easy! :)
Was quite good as I made it, would probably be better if I had adjusted the other ingredients after increasing the shrimp by half a pound
I made this for shrimp tacos on Cinco de Mayo. They were delicious!
Great change from my normal shrimp cooking. Loved the tequila flavor! I actually added rice noodles that I had leftover towards the end. Loved that you can adjust as you like to the recipe.

This was amazing. I followed the suggestion of others and added corn starch but otherwise followed the recipe to a tee. Next time, and there will be a next time, I'll add a little more spice but otherwise, this was wonderful. Served this with Mexican Rice III also from this site. We chopped up the leftovers and had shrimp tacos the next night. Double yummy!
Quick and easy, and so tasty. We served it over rice and it made a wonderful dinner that everyone enjoyed.
I use same recipie , is the best.

This is an awesome recipe for putting in a shrimp Taco. I have also made it for chicken tacos using cut up chicken breasts. I add southwestern salad mix in the wrap with their dressing and some garlic butter rice on the side. It's is spot on for a wonderful taste with flour or corn tortilla's. Thanks for this forever!
